<STRUCT_0001>
The notions considered in this section are not prominently defined in EGA.
A ``universally Japanese scheme'' is mentioned and defined in
<REF_0001>. A ``Japanese scheme'' is mentioned in
<REF_0002> but no definition is given.
A Nagata scheme (as given below) occurs in a few
places in the literature (see for example <REF_0003> and
<REF_0004>).

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
We briefly recall that a domain <MATH_0001> is called <TEXTITOPEN_0001>Japanese<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> if the integral
closure of <MATH_0002> in any finite extension of its fraction field is finite over
<MATH_0003>. A ring <MATH_0004> is called <TEXTITOPEN_0002>universally Japanese<TEXTITCLOSE_0002> if for any finite type
ring map <MATH_0005> with <MATH_0006> a domain <MATH_0007> is Japanese. A ring <MATH_0008> is called
<TEXTITOPEN_0003>Nagata<TEXTITCLOSE_0003> if it is Noetherian and <MATH_0009> is Japanese for every
prime <MATH_0010> of <MATH_0011>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> Assume <MATH_0002> integral. We say <MATH_0003> is <TEXTITOPEN_0001>Japanese<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>
if for every <MATH_0004> there exists an
affine open neighbourhood <MATH_0005> such that the ring
<MATH_0006> is Japanese (see
Algebra, Definition <REF_0001>).
<STRUCT_0003> We say <MATH_0007> is <TEXTITOPEN_0002>universally Japanese<TEXTITCLOSE_0002> if for every <MATH_0008>
there exists an affine open neighbourhood <MATH_0009> such that
the ring <MATH_0010> is universally Japanese (see
Algebra, Definition <REF_0002>).
<STRUCT_0004> We say <MATH_0011> is <TEXTITOPEN_0003>Nagata<TEXTITCLOSE_0003> if for every <MATH_0012> there exists an
affine open neighbourhood <MATH_0013> such that the ring
<MATH_0014> is Nagata (see
Algebra, Definition <REF_0003>).
<STRUCT_0005>
